items.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: It was a collaboration. It’s hard to tell you right now who did which. We worked very well together.

ctx.x: When did you start working with William Grant Still?

On that particular piece. I had known Bill from when he was in this so-called . . . on that hour with Willard Robeson back there in the late ’20s, early ’30s. That Deep River Hour. He did all that writing. He was a . . . he aspired to be a so-called symphony musician. He became, as he says, the first black to lead a symphony orchestra. His daughter, Judy, is still around, pushing his music, pushing him. But anyway, that’s when I met him. But I didn’t . . . never had any idea that I would do anything with him.…
Did he do The Deserted Farm [sic: A Deserted Farm] as well?
